transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Wednesday, November 4. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. US midterms: Indian-origin Pia Dandiya wins Florida House race. Pia Dandiya has made history by winning Florida's 22nd Congressional District race, marking her as the first Indian-American from the state to achieve this milestone. With her roots tracing back to Indian immigrant parents and a strong background in education and public service, she is set to represent a newly refreshed district that spans parts of Palm Beach, Broward, Hendry, and Collier counties. Spain transport minister Óscar Puente quits 6 days after train disaster kills 69. Spain's transport minister Óscar Puente resigned after a high-speed train collision near Madrid caused 69 fatalities. This incident was the second major rail disaster on the Madrid-Seville route in just one year. Following the October 28 crash, Puente faced pressure from opposition politicians and railway unions demanding his resignation. He acknowledged responsibility for the accidents and announced measures to improve railway safety. Starting November 16, Apple's new App Store rule bars minors from certain apps. Apple is set to implement more stringent rules for the App Store on November 16, 2026, particularly for dating applications and AI companions. All such applications will require an 18+ age rating, and developers must submit content descriptors by January 12, 2027. This rollout is part of an initiative to bolster child safety and mitigate privacy issues linked to location-sharing features, impacting many well-known AI companion applications worldwide. Why a desi family is following bid of El-Sayed to make US Senate history. Democrat Abdul El-Sayed is competing against Republican Mike Rogers in the Michigan Senate race. If elected, El-Sayed will become the first Muslim US senator. His wife, Dr. Sarah Jukaku, is connected to Bhatkal, Karnataka, through her heritage. Bihar woman turns village into 'Mushroom Village', empowers 250 women. In Bihar's Nalanda district, Anita Devi ventured into mushroom farming to uplift her family's financial situation. Initially faced with skepticism from her community, her unwavering dedication culminated in the formation of the Madhopur Farmers Producers Company, which by 2025 embraced 512 farmers and provided vital agricultural resources. Devi's initiative has empowered local women and promoted self-sufficiency, with aspirations to expand into diverse produce like makhana. Washington sisters lose fence boundary dispute; court orders one fence removed. Two sisters in Washington, US, lost a property dispute involving fences on both sides of their home after a survey revealed discrepancies in the boundary lines. The Washington Court of Appeals upheld rulings favouring both neighbours, including an order to remove a fence encroaching on one neighbour's land. The court also upheld legal-fee awards and granted the neighbours additional fees for the appeal. Man uses 50-tonne crane to move 100-year-old peepal tree 2 km. Bharat Sisodia and his team moved a 100-year-old peepal tree after it was cut down in Ahmedabad. They found that part of the original root system was still alive and nurtured it. This work emphasized the need for ongoing maintenance and care after transplanting trees. While the tree began to show new growth, it still faced potential threats from development projects. US polls: Indian-American candidates script key wins; Khanna, Bera await verdict. The 2026 US midterm elections are witnessing a growing presence of Indian-American candidates in American politics, with several securing victories in key congressional and state-level contests. Microsoft AI CEO clarifies: I stand by my view that AI does not have rights or feelings. Mustafa Suleyman, the CEO of Microsoft AI, maintains that current AI systems are not conscious and lack rights. He emphasized that credible evidence must be publicly disclosed if AI consciousness is proven. Suleyman argues that creating conscious AI poses risks and suggests halting development if signs of consciousness emerge. He asserts the importance of prioritizing human welfare over the potential creation of conscious digital beings. Georgia city's entire full-time police force quits after mayor tracks chief. A small Georgia city is facing a police staffing crisis after its entire full-time police force resigned. Mayor Craig Timmons admitted placing a GPS tracker on Police Chief Lamar Bunn's truck over concerns about his timesheets. Bunn has denied wrongdoing, while the mass resignations have left the city relying on the county sheriff's office for police coverage. Indian-origin Aruna Miller wins re-election as Maryland lieutenant governor. In a significant electoral event, Aruna Miller was re-elected as Maryland's lieutenant governor in the 2026 midterm elections, partnering with Governor Wes Moore. She successfully outmaneuvered Republican Rob Krop, enhancing Indian-American representation in government. Miller campaigned vigorously on vital issues such as federal immigration and economic policies, calling for voter engagement to challenge the Trump administration's actions, while also pledging to advocate for immigrant community initiatives in Maryland.
